review.summary: The proposal grants PROPOSER_ROLE to a Security Council contract, which contradicts the stated intent of only allowing cancellation of malicious proposals. This creates a direct path for the council to schedule arbitrary TimelockController operations and potentially bypass normal DAO governance.

scenarios.title: Compromised Security Council schedules arbitrary governance actions
preconditions: PROPOSER_ROLE is granted to the Security Council contract
The Security Council contract or its signers are compromised or collude
The TimelockController delay can elapse without cancellation

steps.description: The compromised council uses the granted PROPOSER_ROLE to schedule a malicious TimelockController operation, such as transferring treasury assets or upgrading a critical contract.
After the timelock delay, the scheduled operation is executed without a normal DAO proposal vote.

scenarios.impact: Arbitrary governance actions can be executed by the Security Council, bypassing DAO voting and potentially draining funds or altering protocol control.
scenarios.refutedBy: Not refuted: Deterministic source analysis confirms granted role has schedule() capability on TimelockController.

scenarios.title: Permanent proposer privilege beyond the two-year term
preconditions: The grantRole call does not include an expiration or automatic revocation
No future proposal revokes PROPOSER_ROLE from the council contract

steps.description: PROPOSER_ROLE is granted indefinitely to the Security Council contract.
After the stated term ends in 2028, the contract retains the ability to schedule TimelockController operations unless explicitly revoked.

scenarios.impact: A former or rotated Security Council retains proposer authority indefinitely, increasing long-term governance risk.
scenarios.refutedBy: Not refuted: Deterministic source analysis confirms granted role has schedule() capability on TimelockController.

scenarios.title: Council schedules privilege escalation for itself
preconditions: PROPOSER_ROLE allows scheduling arbitrary TimelockController calls
The council can propose operations that modify its own permissions or the TimelockController configuration
No independent guardian cancels the scheduled operation

steps.description: The council schedules a TimelockController operation granting itself additional roles, such as CANCELLER_ROLE, EXECUTOR_ROLE, or DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
Once executed, the council expands its authority beyond the intended cancellation-only mandate.

scenarios.impact: The Security Council can escalate its own privileges and entrench control over DAO governance execution.
scenarios.refutedBy: Not refuted: Deterministic source analysis confirms granted role has schedule() capability on TimelockController.

items.issue: The proposal motivation states the Security Council has a single power to cancel malicious proposals, but the executable action grants PROPOSER_ROLE, which allows scheduling arbitrary TimelockController operations.
The role grant has no on-chain expiration, so the council contract may retain PROPOSER_ROLE beyond the stated two-year term unless a future proposal explicitly revokes it.

The recipient is a verified contract, but the proposal does not describe its upgradeability, signer set, or compromise-resistance properties, which are critical for a role that can schedule arbitrary governance operations.

findings: Compromised Security Council schedules arbitrary governance actions: not_refuted
Permanent proposer privilege beyond the two-year term: not_refuted
Council schedules privilege escalation for itself: not_refuted
